questions.q: Which statement is a public fact about Zillow Offers?
options: It was wound down, announced in November 2021
It was sold to another company in 2019
It never bought a home
It was shut down because of a software bug in 2015
why: It bought and resold many homes.

questions.q: Expected margin per home is 3%. The price error has a standard deviation of 6%. About what share of trades could lose money if the error is roughly normal and the margin is the mean outcome? (use z = 0.5: share below zero is about 31%)
questions.why: Mean outcome = +3%, sd = 6%, so zero is 0.5 sd below the mean. About 31% of outcomes are below zero.

questions.q: What is adverse selection in this case?
options: Sellers accept mainly the offers that are too high for their home, so the bought sample is biased
The model selects the best features
Buyers choose bad houses at random
Houses become more expensive
why: It is not random; sellers choose.

questions.q: Why can't diversification across 1 000 homes remove the risk of a market turn?
options: Because errors are independent
Because errors are correlated: all prices move together in a regime change
Because homes are all the same
Because the model is too simple
why: Homes differ, but share market-wide shocks.

questions.q: Scenario: your model has a small average error on all listings, but deals you win lose money. What is the first check?
options: Retrain with more layers
Measure bias and calibration on the accepted (traded) sample, not on all listings
Collect nothing
Raise offers
why: More layers do not fix selection bias.
You need more diagnostics, not fewer.
Higher offers would increase adverse selection.

questions.q: Which controls reduce the risk of a company that trades on forecasts? (pick all)
options: Exposure limits per market
Stress tests for a price drop
Offers based on a conservative quantile
Ignore alerts when growth targets are at risk
why: Show the impact of a shock.
This is the opposite of good governance.
